source: CPT–APE founder October 16 rulings and 38-page Doctrinal-Drift Editorial Notes draft
status: partial apparatus; founder lexical/referent clarification added, 63-note draft not fully ratified
source_verification: notes paraphrase editorial positions; separate from actual verse witness

notes.label: The name in the commission
notes.body: Founder editorial direction: invocation is in the name of Yahawah alone, and this commission is not to be treated as a water-baptism instruction. The received manuscript wording and this author-directed adaptation must remain distinguished. The currently displayed source verse may not yet implement this ruling.

notes.label: The Word and Yahawah
notes.body: Yahawashi is distinct from Yahawah and is a created Son who served among the agents of Yahawah's heavenly council. This is the founder's interpretive ruling, not a claim that the surviving Greek manuscripts literally use that full explanation. A final main-text rendering remains an editorial task.

notes.label: Son of God
notes.body: The founder directs the Son of God reading, rather than 'only begotten God.' Manuscript witnesses differ at this passage; preserve their distinctions and document the choice in the final apparatus.

notes.label: Before Abraham
notes.body: The founder understands Yahawashi as existing spiritually before Abraham, not bodily. Avoid an English rendering that turns this into identification with Yahawah in Exodus 3:14. The precise previously accepted short wording still requires reconciliation against the author transcript.

notes.label: Oneness in purpose
notes.body: The founder reads unity as shared purpose and action, not identity of being or a theory of shared divine substance.

notes.label: Thomas and the appointed king
notes.body: The founder directs a royal reading of Thomas's address to Yahawashi, distinct from identifying Yahawashi as Yahawah. Any change to the main text requires transparent editorial identification.

notes.label: Fullness of authority
notes.body: The founder's ruling emphasizes fullness of authority and divine appointment, not a three-person substance or co-identical beings. This is a reading note, not invented manuscript wording.

notes.label: Royal address
notes.body: The founder favors the royal address 'Your throne, O Lord,' with 'Lord' as a kingly title. This is an editorial adaptation, not a claim that the surviving manuscript reads exactly this in English.

notes.label: The true God
notes.body: The founder identifies the true God as Yahawah and distinguishes him from Yahawashi.

notes.label: Young woman
notes.body: The founder chooses 'young woman' for Hebrew almah. The Septuagint's Greek term and later interpretations must be distinguished in the textual notes. Do not conflate the different source traditions.

notes.label: Israel as the suffering servant
notes.body: The founder identifies national Israel as the suffering servant, with Isaiah 41:8, 44:1 and 49:3 providing the covenant context. Retain the singular literary pronouns in the source and explain the collective interpretation in notes; this interpretation does not independently establish the identity of the pierced figure in Zechariah.

notes.label: Yahawah and my lord
notes.body: Distinguish Yahawah from the royal lord or coming anointed intercessor. The speaker's authorship may not be established by the traditional psalm heading alone.

notes.label: The seventy weeks
notes.body: Founder interpretation: this prophecy concerns Israel and Jerusalem, with Second Temple and 70 CE historical context and a possible recurring pattern across later captivities and restorations. The precise relationship to a final week is unresolved; the founder does not believe we are presently in that final week.

notes.label: The pierced one and national mourning
notes.body: The founder considers a messianic figure possible, but does not identify the pierced one definitively with Isaiah 53's servant or Zechariah 13's struck shepherd. Preserve the Hebrew 'me' / 'him' shift as evidence and do not force an identity through translation.

notes.label: Like a lion / pierced
notes.body: This textual reading is not settled. Compare the available Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions before choosing the final wording; do not fabricate agreement between witnesses.

notes.label: Assembly, not institution
notes.body: The October 16 editorial draft flags ekklesia being turned into an institutional 'church.' The proposed terminology is 'assembly.' This note is draft editorial guidance and does not by itself authorize rewriting the main-text witness.

notes.label: Passover terminology
notes.body: The editorial draft distinguishes Greek pascha ('Passover') from the English term 'Easter.' Treat an English festival substitution as a translation question and preserve the underlying witness evidence.

notes.label: Nations and Gentiles: determine the referent by context
notes.source: Founder clarification October 17, 2026, read alongside the October 16 Doctrinal-Drift Editorial Notes draft, especially pp.27 and 36; the draft itself already notes that Israel may be called a nation.
notes.body: Founder clarification: English 'Gentiles' often translates Greek ethnos (singular, 'nation/people') or ethnē (plural, 'nations/peoples'). That is the lexical starting point, not a built-in declaration that everyone so called is a non-Israelite. Israel itself may be called a nation (Luke 7:5); Acts 4:27 contrasts nations with the people of Israel, showing a non-Israelite referent in that context. Matthew 28:19 says 'all nations', and Romans 11:13 addresses a nations/Gentile audience. Prefer rendering the underlying word transparently as nation(s) or people(s) where grammar supports it, but decide whom it identifies passage by passage from speaker, audience and surrounding contrasts. Never automatically claim that every reference is about non-Israelites, or that every reference refers to Israelites. No unreviewed mass-edit of Scripture or invented source wording.

watchlist_status: The draft is labeled a 25-rule watchlist but lists 27 term groups (pp.36–38). Founder clarified 2026-10-17 that nations does not inherently mean non-Israelites; remaining source-proposed substitutions are unratified.
